correctness.rationale: The states track omitted with zero descendant-block selected neighbors, omitted with one, and selected, weighting a vertex only in its selected state. An omitted parent with no selected clique child allows either omitted state for every child; if it has one selected child, other children see that sibling and must have zero selected descendant neighbors. A selected parent allows either all children omitted in their zero states or all children selected; any mixed choice would give an omitted child two selected neighbors. At a vertex the descendant blocks contribute disjoint neighbor sets, so the zero/one calculation and the selected-state product are necessary and sufficient. Induction on the incidence tree gives the root sum, and independent components multiply; bridges, isolates and the empty graph obey the same conventions. The two-accumulator formula evaluates the one-exception sums in linear operations; there are O(|V|) incidence edges after decomposition, hence the claimed O(|V|+|E|) gate bound holds, without claiming linear coefficient-expansion bit-time. In a bouquet an omitted center admits only empty and singleton choices; a selected center permits independent all-or-none choices of each petal, giving exactly the stated polynomial. Independent finite code and output in branches/ebabd826-770f-4a0f-b8d5-5312a62f3776/record5_independent_check.py and record5_independent_check.txt corroborated every coefficient on 123 generated graphs up to 10 vertices and a heterogeneous bouquet; finite checks are not the unrestricted induction. The frozen output counts 8367 nonempty labeled block graphs through order six, with the empty graph outside that tested histogram.

originality.rationale: Demonstrated stronger coverage, not a search miss or an inaccessible-source judgment. Two distinct indexed records give the same three-state positive recurrence with arbitrary individual vertex weights. Substituting one common weight z gives the frozen circuit coefficient by coefficient; the earlier general theorem has an O(|V|) gate bound and explicitly covers disconnected graphs, isolates and the empty graph. The heterogeneous bouquet expression is the direct evaluation of the same covered recurrence on leaf petals, not a distinct structural result. The equal-petal derivation was already explicitly given. No historical authorship or precedence inference beyond the demonstrated mathematical duplication is needed for this assessment.
residual_risks: Several bounded-width and older convexity papers were not inspected in full, so no complete exclusion of additional precedence is made. This does not weaken the explicit stronger-circuit coverage already established.
The heterogeneous formula need not appear verbatim in the compared records: the demonstrated specialization proves it mechanically.
